title: NGC 6188
caption: The emission nebula NGC 6188, photographed by J. Pérez for ESO

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The nebula NGC 6188 glows red in this photograph. The color comes from hydrogen gas, lit up by massive stars that formed recently. The nebula lies in the southern constellation Ara (the Altar), some 4000 light-years away.

NGC 6188 is an emission nebula, a cloud of gas that shines with its own light because nearby hot stars energize it. It sits inside a large, dark molecular cloud. Clouds like that are dense and cold, and they are where new stars are born.

The ultraviolet light of hot young stars is what makes hydrogen in nebulae like this one shine, and the red glow is the typical color of that hydrogen emission. The photograph is credited to J. Pérez and ESO.
scale: NGC 6188 is some 4000 light-years away, according to ESO.

understand.summary: ESO does not name the telescope, camera or filters. The red color is emission from hydrogen.
understand.eye: The nebula is too faint for the eye to see in color, and a camera exposure gathers far more light.
